Datadog’s Response to OpenSSL Vulnerabilities
Copy link
Vulnerabilities
January 27, 2026

In response to OpenSSL’s official advisory published on January 27, 2026 regarding twelve (12) vulnerabilities, Datadog triggered its incident response process to assess exposure, validate detections, and coordinate remediation. We identified affected OpenSSL versions in a limited set of components, including the Datadog Agent, and will deploy fixes promptly in accordance with our standard vulnerability remediation SLAs, following required validation and staged rollout procedures.

Customers should review OpenSSL’s official advisory and apply applicable patches in their own environments. At this time, we have no reports of widespread exploitation and will continue to monitor and provide updates if we identify material changes.

Datadog's Response to React Server Component’s RCE Vulnerability (CVE-2025-55182)
Copy link
Vulnerabilities
December 4, 2025

In response to the recently disclosed React Server Components vulnerability, CVE-2025-55182, Datadog security conducted an investigation and confirmed that we are not impacted. However, we suggest customers refer to our Research Feed and Security Labs blog post for guidance to assess potential exposure and take the suggested mitigations to secure their applications.

Datadog's Response to Shai-Hulud Worm Campaign
Copy link
Vulnerabilities
November 26, 2025

Since the Shai-Hulud worm campaign affecting NPM packages began in September 2025, we have been assessing our own environment for impact and have confirmed that Datadog has not been impacted by the initial iteration nor the most recent Shai-Hulud 2.0 worm campaign. We have implemented detections for the worm, and are continuously monitoring for infected packages and reviewing potential usage at Datadog. Independent of this campaign, Datadog also proactively monitors for exposure of customer Datadog credentials, such as API and Application keys, and notifies impacted customers.

2025 Penetration Test
Copy link
Compliance
September 5, 2025

We’re pleased to announce that summaries of the 2025 penetration tests for Datadog, Cloudcraft, and CoScreen (performed by NCC Group), as well as Metaplane (performed by Cobalt Group), are available on our security portal. These summaries are accompanied by Letters of Assessment.

Datadog's Response to Salesloft Drift Breach
Copy link
Incidents
September 3, 2025

We conducted an internal investigation and confirmed there is no direct impact to Datadog from the Salesloft Drift breach. Datadog has never installed or used any Salesloft integration, including Drift.

We are actively engaging with our vendors to assess any potential indirect impact through our supply chain.

If we are vulnerable, we intend to patch our environment in adherence with our Vulnerability Management process. Our process and remediation timelines are outlined in our Vulnerability Management at Datadog white paper, which is available via our Trust Portal.\n\nIn the context of customer installed code, the [Datadog Synthetics Private Location Worker container image](https://hub.docker.com/r/datadog/synthetics-private-location-worker) has an affected version of `libcups` installed in the container. This image is not exploitable if configured using Datadog’s default or [recommended configurations](https://docs.datadoghq.com/synthetics/platform/private_locations/configuration/?tab=docker). Datadog has patched the affected image. Additionally, our environment is not publicly accessible via SSH. As such, we consider the vulnerability fully mitigated within the Datadog environment. \n\nTo check if your systems are vulnerable and guidance on how to remediate any affected systems, please refer to Datadog’s recent Security Labs blog post: [RegreSSHion vulnerability CVE-2024-6387: Overview, detection, and remediation](https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/regresshion-vulnerability-cve-2024-6387-overview-detection-and-remediation/).","createdAt":"2024-07-08T20:21:53.747Z","updatedAt":"2024-07-08T20:22:02.212Z","isGlobalProduct":true,"products":[],"spAudience":"public","topicId":"1330a334-bd39-4c38-ae14-a2e11edc9fbf"}]},{"id":"3fe6247b-b179-4460-ae5c-78f79c417cfe","subject":"Datadog's Response to Attacks Against Snowflake Customers","hidden":false,"isPinned":false,"category":"vulnerabilities","createdAt":"2024-05-31T22:00:31.367Z","updatedAt":"2024-06-18T00:38:30.982Z","updates":[{"id":"a9467c41-16d9-40e7-932c-a8dabed51397","message":"In May 2024, [Mandiant notified Snowflake of unauthorized access to certain customer accounts](https://community.snowflake.com/s/question/0D5VI00000Emyl00AB/detecting-and-preventing-unauthorized-user-access). It was determined that this access did not stem from a breach of Snowflake’s enterprise environment, but rather compromised customer credentials. \n\nWe deployed our internal Detection and Response teams to search for signs of impact, and after a thorough investigation, it was determined that there was no impact to Datadog. \n\nAs an added precaution, we have successfully rotated or deleted keys for Snowflake service accounts.","createdAt":"2024-05-31T22:11:22.664Z","updatedAt":"2024-06-18T00:38:30.982Z","isGlobalProduct":true,"products":[],"spAudience":"public","topicId":"3fe6247b-b179-4460-ae5c-78f79c417cfe"}]},{"id":"6df88f9d-00ef-4bb7-bcce-2cb93090d5e1","subject":"Datadog's Response to Sisense Breach","hidden":false,"isPinned":false,"category":"vulnerabilities","createdAt":"2024-04-16T16:55:47.651Z","updatedAt":"2024-06-18T00:38:39.159Z","updates":[{"id":"adce24ad-99dc-4851-a3ba-b14410137eb3","message":"We're aware of [Sisense's breach disclosure](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2024/04/11/compromise-sisense-customer-data). We're not a customer of their platform so we have no direct impact. However, just like most companies are, we're still in the process of reaching out to all of our critical third-parties to identify any potential exposure from them. So far, we have not discovered any.  ","createdAt":"2024-04-16T17:06:14.022Z","updatedAt":"2024-06-18T00:38:39.159Z","isGlobalProduct":true,"products":[],"spAudience":"public","topicId":"6df88f9d-00ef-4bb7-bcce-2cb93090d5e1"}]},{"id":"132b6650-51bb-4d27-ac7e-705b449c62da","subject":"Datadog's Response to liblzma backdoor vulnerability CVE-2024-3094","hidden":false,"isPinned":false,"category":"vulnerabilities","createdAt":"2024-03-29T23:28:38.141Z","updatedAt":"2024-03-29T23:35:24.629Z","updates":[{"id":"63a9a5cf-707a-4a65-aafb-52fa0ff6d59b","message":"On March 29, 2024, we became aware of a backdoor vulnerability liblzma [CVE-2024-3094] and promptly investigated all of our environments against this new threat. After thorough investigation, we found no vulnerable versions anywhere in our environment. \n\nAdditional resources:\n\nGlobal announcement - OSS Security Notification: \nhttps://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2024/03/29/4 \nhttps://access.redhat.com/security/cve/CVE-2024-3094\n\nLink to CSM Security Center notification:  \nhttps://app.datadoghq.com/security/csm?panels=security-center%7Cscp-singleton%7CsecurityCardId%3A27\u0026sort=\u0026timestamp=1711753804867\u0026live=true\n\nLink to CSM Vulnerabilities explorer:\nhttps://app.datadoghq.com/security/csm/vm?query=status%3AOpen%20cve%3ACVE-2024-3094%20\u0026group=vulnerability \n","createdAt":"2024-03-29T23:55:40.722Z","updatedAt":"2024-03-29T23:55:40.722Z","isGlobalProduct":true,"products":[],"spAudience":"public","topicId":"132b6650-51bb-4d27-ac7e-705b449c62da"}]},{"id":"8235ce67-8bd2-43ab-a69f-4f68f199a68a","subject":"Datadog's Response to Leaky Vessels Vulnerability","hidden":false,"isPinned":false,"category":"vulnerabilities","createdAt":"2024-02-07T19:40:17.784Z","updatedAt":"2024-02-07T19:40:17.784Z","updates":[{"id":"0a92671c-ddd7-4770-a0bb-fb59ea356d33","message":"Datadog is actively investigating the presence of one of the “Leaky Vessels” vulnerabilities (CVE-2024-21626) and working on patching our container environments identified as vulnerable.
